name: Midland Terminal, Victor (engine and coach at a frame station)
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: Library: 'View of Midland Terminal engine with coal tender and passenger car at station, Victor'; title hand-written on the back of the print; signs read in part '... Express' and '... room'. Looked at before use: the end of a clapboarded frame building with a bracketed gable and a barred window, a boardwalk, four men in overcoats, an engine and one coach, snow. No caption or mark on the copy. The building is frame, not the brick depot of the later views: which building this is has not been worked out, so it is not tied to the depot record.

name: Victor, Colo. from Portland Mine, No. 12
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: Library: bird's-eye view from the Portland mine showing the dump of its tunnel, the Midland Terminal depot, the Victor Hotel, the Gold Coin mine, and a 'Midland Terminal or Florence & Cripple Creek' engine and cars; from a copy negative of a cabinet card. Looked at before use: the town from high on the north-east, snow on the far hills; an engine under steam on a curving track at the left edge of town; a dump and a timber structure in the foreground. Lettered on the negative by the photographer: 'Victor, Colo. from Portland Mine', 'No. 12', a tunnel name, and 'Yelton'. Those are the maker's own, so nothing needs cropping. The depot was not picked out by this project.

name: R. R. war in front of Strong mine
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: Library: 'the district yards for the Florence and Cripple Creek Railroad in Victor ... rail cars toppled on the tracks probably during a price war between the F. & C. C. R. and the Colorado Springs and Cripple Creek District Railway.' That explanation is the cataloguer's guess; the Short Line was not built until 1901 (secondary), so the two do not fit, and what happened is not established here. Looked at before use: a yard below a mine with three stacks; a box car on its side with a crowd round it; an engine at the left; a timber truss bridge over the tracks; the title lettered on the negative along the bottom. No other mark.

name: View of Victor
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: Library: from the hillside near the Midland Terminal station; 'Midland Terminal depot with gondolas & box cars, and Florence & Cripple Creek railroad line (possibly) on hillside'; title printed on the front of the print. Looked at before use: the business district from the north, with brick blocks, the Mary Cashen headframe (its name painted on the shaft house) and, at the lower right, lines of box cars standing among sheds below a small hip-roofed building. The copy shows no printed title, so nothing needs cropping. Which building is the depot was not settled by this project.

name: Union Depot, Victor, Colo. (postcard)
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: Library: a postcard, 'Published by H. H. Rosser, Victor, Colo.'; 'Research indicates that this is the Midland Terminal Railroad Depot in Victor, Colorado, built in 1895'. Looked at before use: a brick station with round-arched openings, a wide hipped roof and a conical-roofed bay, men on the platform, track in front, a headframe behind. The card's own printed title and publisher's line are part of the original. The building matches the brick depot of X-546 and X-547. Why a card of about 1902 calls it a union depot is not known.

name: Buildings at Victor, with Midland Terminal car 322
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: Library: frame buildings with tracks in front; a car lettered 'M.T.RY 322'; an ink note on the back, as the library transcribes it: 'Frank Cochrans H.G. office Victor opesate [sic] M.T. Depot.' Looked at before use: a low clapboarded building with wooden steps down to a track, a two-storey house behind with people on its porch, a box car lettered M.T.RY 322 at the left, a mine dump on the skyline. No mark on the image. The note on the back suggests it stood opposite the depot; that has not been tested.

name: Victor and Battle Mountain
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: Library: 'Snowy hillside with many tree stumps overlooking town identified as Victor'; 'Victor F&CCR' and '186' printed on the bottom; a note on the back says it continues another print marked 'Weeks Photo'. name: Old Midland Terminal station at Victor
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: Library: 'a one-story brick building with medium pitch hip roof, two chimneys, wide projecting eaves, brackets, top of short conical tower & finial, semi-circular arched windows ... gondola car filled with debris'. Looked at before use: the brick depot from the track side and one end: three round-arched windows and an arched doorway, a gondola on a track in front loaded with rock, mine dumps behind. No mark on the copy.
